title: ChatGPT Enterprise Lands on AWS Marketplace
summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace on Nov 9, 2026. AWS customers can now buy it through existing billing. What it means for enterprise AI adoption.

AWS Marketplace


# ChatGPT Enterprise Lands on AWS Marketplace


By OpenTools Team


·


November 10, 2026


OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise available through AWS Marketplace on Monday, letting companies buy the workplace AI suite through their existing AWS billing. The move cuts procurement friction for enterprises and allows eligible spending to count toward AWS commitments.


## One-Click Procurement for ChatGPT Enterprise


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) made ChatGPT Enterprise available through AWS Marketplace on Monday, giving organizations a new way to buy the workplace AI suite without signing a separate contract. AWS customers can now purchase ChatGPT Enterprise — including ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots — through their existing AWS purchasing and billing relationship, with eligible spending counting toward AWS Enterprise Discount Program (EDP) or Private Pricing Agreement (PPA) commitments,[OpenAI announced](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-aws-marketplace/) .


“Enterprises want to put AI to work across their teams without adding new layers of procurement,” said Matt Yanchyshyn, Vice President of AWS Marketplace and Partner Services at AWS, in the announcement. “With ChatGPT Enterprise in AWS Marketplace, customers can buy it through their AWS account, govern it alongside the rest of their software spend, and move from evaluation to rollout faster.”


OpenAI’s Chris Grusz, Managing Director of Cloud Partnerships, added: “Joint customers can now bring ChatGPT to their teams through the cloud provider they already trust,”[according to OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-aws-marketplace/) .


## Why This Matters: Procurement Is the Real AI Bottleneck


For large enterprises, buying software isn’t just about picking the best product — it’s about legal reviews, security assessments, budget allocation, and vendor onboarding. Adding a new vendor can take months. By listing ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) bypasses much of this friction: the vendor relationship already exists, the billing is pre-approved, and the spend applies to committed cloud budgets.


Sophos CTO John Peterson captured this in the announcement: “Having the option to buy through a single channel and apply existing AWS commitments removes friction that often slows enterprise AI adoption. Time that would otherwise go to procurement can go toward using AI to deliver more value for our customers,”[according to OpenAI’s announcement](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-aws-marketplace/) .


## AWS + OpenAI: The Partnership Deepens


Matt Yanchyshyn, AWS Marketplace VP, framed the move around procurement simplicity,[per OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-aws-marketplace/) . This listing is the latest step in[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) ’s accelerating relationship with AWS. In November 2025, OpenAI signed a multi-year, $38 billion compute agreement with AWS,[per OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-aws-marketplace/) . In April 2026, the companies introduced OpenAI models in[Amazon](https://opentools.ai/organizations/amazon) Bedrock, Codex on AWS, and Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI. The Marketplace listing adds the final piece: letting enterprises buy the finished ChatGPT product through the same channel they use for infrastructure.


The timing is notable. OpenAI just closed $11 billion in new funding at a $1.25 trillion valuation, and the company claims more than 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week. Making the enterprise version available through AWS Marketplace is a distribution play designed to convert that consumer-scale awareness into enterprise revenue — without the slow procurement cycles that typically gate enterprise software deals.


> "Enterprises want to put AI to work across their teams without adding new layers of procurement. With ChatGPT Enterprise in AWS Marketplace, customers can buy it through their AWS account, govern it alongside the rest of their software spend, and move from evaluation to rollout faster."


**Matt Yanchyshyn** - Vice President, AWS Marketplace and Partner Services, AWS


## What’s Available and What’s Not


The Marketplace listing covers the full ChatGPT Enterprise suite: ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots.[OpenAI says](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-aws-marketplace/) customers get “the same models, features, and functionality available directly from[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) , with new features released at the same time.” Eligible customers can also access ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Financial Services through the Marketplace.


Importantly, this is a procurement channel change, not a product change. AWS handles purchasing and billing; OpenAI continues to manage the product experience. The Marketplace listing complements — rather than replaces — OpenAI models in[Amazon](https://opentools.ai/organizations/amazon) Bedrock, which developers use to build AI applications and agents,[per the AWS Marketplace listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-sscra4m7iracg) . Organizations can now use Bedrock for custom AI development and ChatGPT Enterprise for team productivity, all through one AWS bill.


## The Microsoft Dynamic: AWS Gets the Sale, Not Just the Infrastructure


The AWS Marketplace listing is strategically significant because it gives AWS a direct sales role for[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's flagship enterprise product — not just the cloud infrastructure underneath it. This deepens the OpenAI-AWS relationship at a time when OpenAI's historic partnership with[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) has been restructured. In April 2026, OpenAI wrote about[“the next phase of the Microsoft OpenAI partnership”](https://openai.com/index/next-phase-of-microsoft-partnership) in a blog post that signaled a shift from exclusivity. The AWS Marketplace listing turns that shift into a concrete distribution channel.


For enterprises already committed to AWS, the calculus is simple: ChatGPT Enterprise is now just another line item on the AWS bill, with no new vendor onboarding, no separate procurement process, and spend that counts toward existing cloud commitments. For OpenAI, it's a channel that converts AWS's massive enterprise customer base into ChatGPT Enterprise subscribers with minimal sales friction.
